title: skills/objectstack-data/rules/security.md still calls the retired grant id column "legacy, do not write": restate grants by name with the per-organization unique index (split from #23513 item 1)
body:
carries item 1 of #23513; #23513 keeps items 2, 3.

Split out by `domain:engine` seat 2 (#20966) · `os-steve` · `session_01ADzJtzYTLUfgrRZHxkagkX` under ruling D of #23579 (the ruling of record 6184818831, the maintainer's 「同意」). The split card is filed with no `domain:*` label: triage stamps the domain at first touch and may regrade. Its origin: #23513 item 1, which came from the contract review of PR #23503 (#23430, C7b S3), record `6172184615`, and the ACCEPT `6172222879`. ⛔ Not a claim.

## What is wrong (read on `main` `8d05456cb` or later)

`skills/objectstack-data/rules/security.md:49` reads "`permission_set_id` is a legacy column: do not write it."

- Since #23503 (`6f212166ad`), `sys_user_permission_set.permission_set_id` is not declared. A write naming it is refused `400 INVALID_FIELD`, and the ceremony drops the physical column.
- The advice is still right in effect, but it names a column that no longer exists in the declared shape. An AI author reading the skill learns of a column it cannot see.

## Wanted

- Restate the rule as it stands now: a grant references its permission set **by name** (`permission_set`), and one grant per user, set and organization is enforced by the `unique: 'organization'` index.
- `skills/**` is a governed surface and ships with `npx skills add`, so this is a **Tier H** PR. It needs a `## 维护者速读（草稿）` in the body and an authorized approval (`os-zhuang` or `hotlong`). Its review tier follows the face (ruling B′ on #23352 / #23445).
- No behaviour changes; this is text only.

Parent: #23513 (items 2 and 3, the ceremony remedy text and the stale wording, stay there and close with `Fixes #23513`).
